acceptanceItems.text: Real Bastrop tenant/persona, with a live-verified cross-tenant read refusal.
acceptanceItems.how: bastrop_tx/staff registered in src/actors.mjs (orgId matches the existing CODE_BOOKS['BASTROP-UDC'] convention). engagementCrossTenantRefusal wired ahead of every route nested under /api/plan-review/engagements/:id, keyed on the x-persona header the QA UI already sends on every request (backend.js was silently dropping it before this change; now forwards it). Live-verified against the DEPLOYED production service, both directions: bastrop_tx reading a template-city engagement -> 403; the reverse -> 403; matching-tenant -> 200; no-persona-asserted -> 200 (unchanged). Beyond the check's literal ask: also verified live that a cross-tenant WRITE (POST /edition) is refused the same way, since the check is method-agnostic (keyed on a header, not the body).

acceptanceItems.text: Live query path from IBC2018P6 to the real substrate content; IPMC2018P2 left honest-empty.
acceptanceItems.how: resolveCodeLookup computes a live DID for any digits-and-dots section number against IBC2018P6 and hands it to server.mjs, which verifies it via get_atom with the already-provisioned HAUSKA_MCP_PLATFORM_KEY and classifies the result three ways (resolved / absent-verified / not-entitled / source-unavailable) via the new classifyLiveSectionFetch. Live-verified against the DEPLOYED production service: section 1001.1 resolves with a real citation, heading, and deep link sourced from the atom itself; section 9999.9 (well-formed, nonexistent) returns absent-verified; an IRC-shaped input (R311.7) stays a pure, no-network unchecked absence exactly as before. IPMC2018P2 confirmed unchanged (two independent live signals: hauska-mcp-server's own plan_review_get_code tool describes 'IPMC is a typed absence', and targeted get_atom probes found nothing).

incidentalFix.what: get_atom's real response nests section fields one level deeper than this route's existing payload extraction reached (`data.atom.title`, not `data.title`). The already-shipped Bastrop UDC citation path (G-108) had been silently falling back to source-unavailable in production since it shipped, for every real section, because of this.
incidentalFix.evidence: Curled the LIVE DEPLOYED production revision for BASTROP-UDC/14-02-003 before writing any fix: returned typed-absence source-unavailable. After this fix's deploy, the same URL returns a resolved citation with real body, heading and deep link.
incidentalFix.whyInScope: The new IBC live path shares the identical extraction code; without this fix, item 4's own check ('returns a genuine ... citation ... not typed absence for a section that actually exists') could not have passed regardless of the new wiring. A one-line extraction-order correction, not a restructuring -- folded into this change rather than filed separately.

incidentalCitationFix: iccDeepLink now prefers the atom's own verbatimTextDeepLink/sourceUrl (real, licence-provided) over a hand-built template (`.../content/<bookId>/<section>`) that had been dead code until this change and was never checked against the real codes.iccsafe.org URL form -- confirmed live that the template's URL shape disagrees with the atom's own, correct one.
substrateFindingNotFixed: list_jurisdictions/query_jurisdiction report icc-model-code and bastrop_tx as accessPolicy 'public-free' at the jurisdiction-rollup level, but per-atom get_atom enforcement refuses BOTH anonymously (confirmed on both a real ICC atom and a real Bastrop UDC atom). Two independently derived signals disagree. Not this repo's defect (hauska-mcp-server is substrate-seat owned); named for the substrate seat, not corrected here.

cloudRun.trafficIssueFoundAndFixed: The bare --source deploy created and readied the new revision (confirmed via `gcloud run revisions describe`: Ready=True) but did NOT shift traffic to it -- latestReadyRevisionName and the 100% traffic slot both still pointed at the OLD revision (00021-huc) after the deploy command reported success, because this service pins traffic to explicit named revisions/tags rather than auto-following latest (every existing revision in the traffic list carries a canary tag, e.g. g112-recon). Corrected with `gcloud run services update-traffic plan-review --to-revisions=plan-review-00014-bbg=100`, then re-verified traffic was 100% on the new revision by reading the JSON traffic array by field name, not the CLI's own summary line (which had misleadingly named the OLD revision as 'deployed and serving').

LESSON: This plan-review Cloud Run service pins traffic to named/tagged revisions rather than auto-following 'latest'. A bare `gcloud run deploy --source` here creates and readies a new revision but does NOT shift traffic to it -- an explicit `gcloud run services update-traffic --to-revisions=<new>=100` is required afterward. The deploy command's own final summary line is misleading in this state: it names the OLD, still-serving revision as 'deployed and serving 100 percent of traffic', not the one it just built. Verify by reading the traffic array by field name (JSON), never the CLI summary text.

get_atom's real response body nests section fields one level deeper than a first read of the JSON-RPC envelope suggests: {"data":{"atom":{"title":...}}}, not {"data":{"title":...}}. A shallow `atom?.data || atom?.atom || atom` extraction looks plausible and silently never matches a real atom. Verified by curling the live substrate directly for two independent atom types (a real IBC section and the already-shipped Bastrop UDC section) before touching any code.

A well-formed-but-nonexistent DID against hauska-mcp-server's get_atom returns a clean 200 {"data":{"atom":null},...,"meta":{"note":"No atom found..."}}, not an error and not a thrown exception -- a positive determination worth its own typed-absence kind (absent-verified), distinct from a genuine fetch failure (source-unavailable) or an accessPolicy denial (not-entitled, itself a distinct, matchable string: "is not readable under the caller's accessPolicy").
